### Architect · Answer

Event: `81deeb2bd335b8c779fb6d8e8fcf5008` · 2026-10-16T11:52:50Z

> Ruling (full text: .wash/local/STEWARD3B-ruling.md). Build from it.
> 
> Q1, the wire: accepted as proposed. `3 approval_opened(key, console: handle[0], reader: handle[1]) -> channel`; the server resolves the principal from the key id (approval keys, then login keys so the core's guard says bad_key, else "" -> unknown); `5 pending -> -`; 6/7 unchanged, the three on badge 2 as the steward's own minted send right (reword steward.md's 'handed in the manifest' for it); `18 approval_waiting` on the notices endpoint, printed `[an approval is waiting]`, badge 1 only. State with it: the reader-thread count is the core's cap on open channels (name the constant; pool stack size), and the pair cannot deadlock because the main loop never waits on a reader (its screen writes are bounded): say so in the doc comment.
> 
> Q4: accepted, the scope stated whole: a labelled lease's `/project` is its label set's vault, whole (fresh, root, the vault's own quota; no sizes.agent.quota carve for it); agents.md's sentence in the file.
> 
> Q2: accepted; bound the reader's line length (a line longer than the parser's longest form is refused, not read further).
> 
> Q3: accepted with one change: a person cannot type 64 hex reliably. The screen shows beside the full hash its first 8 hex as the code; the server accepts the full hash or the code, expanding the code from the last screen it wrote on that channel (the only place it can come from); anything not on the last screen is HashMismatch to the channel only (C9). The core's Approve still takes the full hash; nothing of the core moves. Say why on sshd.md's approve@box paragraph.
> 
> Q5: accepted (a testbench change with its host test and a testbench.md line). Q6: accepted; the case follows the core's rule (the agent's share is 1 beside alice's two sessions: its second note is cap) and its description says so.
